title: attention
content_html:
attention

What does the eye return to after its first pass over an image? A marginal detail might take over, or looking for one thing might make something else disappear. In 10,000, a single dot of colour, the space around it and the arrangement as a whole draw the eye in different ways. The same image may already look different a day later. Does knowing what to look for change what else becomes visible? 10,000

Reading note. Buddhism. The Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta directs attention to the arising and passing of what we observe. Looking at an image has its own shifts of attention. A detail comes forward, holds the eye for a time and then gives way to something else. What changes when those shifts become noticeable? Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta, MN 10
